blurb: Binomial coefficients at graduate level: identities, Newton's series, Lucas, Kummer, q-analogues, Catalan, asymptotics.

pics.alt: The first 32 rows of Pascal's triangle, with odd entries shaded black and even entries white, forming a Sierpinski triangle pattern
pics.caption: Rows 0 to 31 of Pascal's triangle with the odd coefficients shaded black: by Lucas' theorem the odd entries form a discrete approximation of the Sierpinski triangle. The colour of each numeral records the coefficient modulo 4: black for 0, white for 1, red for 2 and yellow for 3.
pics.title: Sierpinski Pascal triangle.svg

pics.alt: Black-and-white photographic portrait of the German mathematician Ernst Eduard Kummer
pics.caption: Ernst Eduard Kummer (1810–1893), whose 1852 theorem states that the power of a prime p dividing C(n, k) equals the number of carries when k and n − k are added in base p.
pics.title: Ernst Eduard Kummer.jpg
